hints: Differentiate with respect to $\theta$ using the chain rule, multiplying by $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\theta}[\cos\theta] = -\sin\theta$.
walkthrough:
Apply the chain rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\theta}[u^n] = n u^{n-1} \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}\theta}$ with $u = \cos\theta$ and $n = -3$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = -3(\cos\theta)^{-4} \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\theta}[\cos\theta]$$

Express $\dfrac{1}{\cos^4\theta}$ as $\sec^4\theta$ to reach the required identity:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = 3\sin\theta\sec^4\theta$$

ai_rubric.Differentiation: Uses correct chain rule with factor $-3\cos^2\theta$ (or $-3(\cos\theta)^{-4}$) and $-\sin\theta$ (M1). Obtains $3\sin\theta\sec^4\theta$ from full correct working (A1).

skill_tags: Applying Initial Conditions to Differential Equations

hints: Separate variables in the differential equation to obtain $\int \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos^4\theta}\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \int \dfrac{x + 3}{x^2 + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x$.
Use part (a) to integrate the $\theta$-term, and split the $x$-integral into $\dfrac{x}{x^2 + 9} + \dfrac{3}{x^2 + 9}$ to obtain $\ln$ and $\arctan$ terms.
Substitute initial conditions $x = 3, \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ to evaluate constant $C$.
Set $x = 0$, evaluate $\sec^3\theta$, and deduce $\cos\theta$ correct to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Multiply both sides by $3$ to use the result of part (a):
$$\int \dfrac{3\sin\theta}{\cos^4\theta}\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \int \dfrac{3(x + 3)}{x^2 + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate the left-hand side using part (a):
$$\int 3\sin\theta\sec^4\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \sec^3\theta$$

Split the right-hand side integral into two standard forms:
$$\int \dfrac{3x + 9}{x^2 + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x = \int \dfrac{3x}{x^2 + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x + \int \dfrac{9}{x^2 + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x$$
- Logarithmic term:
  $$\int \dfrac{3x}{x^2 + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{3}{2}\int \dfrac{2x}{x^2 + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{3}{2}\ln(x^2 + 9)$$
- Inverse tangent term:
  $$\int \dfrac{9}{x^2 + 3^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = 9\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right) = 3\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$$

Assemble the general solution with integration constant $C$:
$$\sec^3\theta = \dfrac{3}{2}\ln(x^2 + 9) + 3\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + C$$

Determine constant $C$ using the initial condition $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ when $x = 3$:
$$\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies \sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 2 \implies \sec^3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 2^3 = 8$$
$$\dfrac{3}{2}\ln(3^2 + 9) = \dfrac{3}{2}\ln(18)$$
$$3\arctan\left(\dfrac{3}{3}\right) = 3\arctan(1) = 3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$$
$$8 = \dfrac{3}{2}\ln(18) + \dfrac{3\pi}{4} + C \implies C = 8 - \dfrac{3\pi}{4} - \dfrac{3}{2}\ln(18)$$

ai_rubric.Applying Initial Conditions to Different: Separates variables correctly (B1). Obtains term of form $p\sec^3\theta$ (B1). Splits $x$ integral into logarithmic and arctan terms (M1). Obtains $q\ln(x^2+9)$ and $r\arctan(x/3)$ (DM1). Obtains $\sec^3\theta = \frac{3}{2}\ln(x^2+9) + 3\arctan(x/3) + C$ (A1). Evaluates constant using $x=3, \theta=\pi/3$ (M1). Obtains $C = 8 - \frac{3\pi}{4} - \frac{3}{2}\ln 18$ (A1). Obtains $\cos\theta = 0.601$ (A1).
